introduction: LIHEAP helps eligible households with home energy costs through state, territory and Tribal programs. Local agencies determine application windows, available assistance and eligibility.

who: Your administering program checks household eligibility using its income or qualifying-benefit rules. Priorities and available funding vary; a low income alone does not guarantee an award.
sections.get: Assistance may address heating or cooling expenses and an energy crisis. Ask your local program which assistance is open for your situation.
sections.docs: Have the utility account, bill, any disconnection notice and household income information ready. Ask the intake agency about other required evidence and explain the date of an impending shutoff.
sections.apply: Use the LIHEAP household eligibility and agency search or state application information to identify the administering office. Apply through that office.
sections.after: Confirm that your application reached the agency and ask how to track it. A pending request does not itself stop a utility disconnection; contact the utility about the deadline and available payment arrangements.

• LIHEAP household search

faqs: Do I apply directly to the federal government?
Applications go through the administering state, territory, Tribal or local program.
Is assistance open all year everywhere?
Application windows and available funding vary locally.
What if I have a shutoff notice?
Tell the intake agency immediately and ask about crisis assistance; also contact the utility.
Does applying guarantee the bill will be paid?
No. The local program must determine eligibility and funding availability.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
